questions.q: Which of these elements can have a fault path attached?
options: Get Records, Create Records, Update Records, Delete Records, and Action elements
Only Decision elements
Only Loop elements
Any element, including Assignment and Display Text
questions.explain: Fault paths attach to elements that can fail at run time against the org: Get/Create/Update/Delete Records and Action elements.

questions.q: A Create Records element has no fault path, and the create fails because a required field is blank. What does the user see?
options: The flow silently skips the element and continues
A generic, unhelpful 'unhandled fault' error
The flow automatically retries the create
An email is sent to the Salesforce admin
questions.explain: Without a fault path, a failing element throws an unhandled fault — a generic error shown to the user, with no useful detail.

questions.q: What does the $Flow.FaultMessage global variable contain?
options: A list of every element in the flow
The flow's version number
The actual system-generated error text for the most recent fault
The name of the user who built the flow
questions.explain: $Flow.FaultMessage holds the real error — e.g. REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING — not a paraphrase, which is why it's worth surfacing.

questions.q: Where do you attach a fault path to an element on the canvas?
options: In Setup, under Process Automation Settings
From the element's own context menu, alongside Copy, Cut, and Delete Element
Only by editing the flow's XML directly
It's attached automatically to every element by default
questions.explain: Add Fault Path appears in the same context menu as Copy Element, Cut Element, and Delete Element.

questions.q: A fault path shows the user a generic 'something went wrong, please try again' message and does nothing else. What's the risk in this approach?
options: There is no risk — this is the recommended pattern
It will cause a governor limit error
It fixes the crash but hides the real problem, so the same fault keeps recurring unnoticed
It automatically deactivates the flow
questions.explain: Swallowing the fault without surfacing $Flow.FaultMessage to someone who can act on it means the underlying cause never gets fixed.
